tests.name: Email A/B Test: Lantern-Led vs. Employer-Led
tests.quarter: UNCLEAR - not explicitly dated or listed in Q1/Q2 summaries
tests.summary: 202,844 emails across 3 variants (Lantern-Led, Employer-Led, Control). Tests open/click/conversion rates by send strategy.
tests.recommendation: Adopt Employer-Led framing as the default send strategy. It delivered the highest open rate (23.24%, +3.63pp over Control) and the highest click rate (1.41%, +0.19pp over Lantern-Led). Conversions were statistically flat across all three variants, so the lift is concentrated in upper-funnel engagement.
tests.notes: Control variant contains no click-through CTA, hence 0.00% click rate. Directional results; conversion sample sizes (48–53) too small for significance testing.
tests.quarterNote: Not found by name in Historical Testing Log across any quarter sheet (Q4 2025–Q4 2026) — still unresolved; may be an ad hoc/unlisted test.

tests.name: NC Window Envelope Test (Large vs. Small Window)
tests.summary: Large Window vs. Small Window envelope. 28-day pre/post analysis. Call rate & case rate per piece mailed.
tests.recommendation: The Large Window envelope is the stronger performer. The 11% relative improvement in call lift is statistically significant, and groups were properly randomized. With both window types costing 10 cents per envelope, we recommend the Large Window format as the go-forward standard, with an expectation of a positive return on no net-new investment.
tests.methodology: 28-day pre/post mailing analysis. DiD = Difference-in-Differences. Both groups statistically equivalent pre-mailing.
tests.logCrossRef: Historical Testing Log, Q1 2026 sheet, Test #2: "Small vs Large Window Envelope Test", Direct Mail, Start 2026-01-16, End 2026-02-13, Status: Results Published.

tests.name: Email Timing Test: Send Before vs. After ID Card
tests.summary: 165,255 total members. Iterable data collected 1 week after send. Opens, clicks & conversions comparison.
tests.analysis: Sending after the ID Card drove significantly higher open rates, jumping nearly 4 percentage points (+19% relative). Click rate held steady at 0.69% in both groups, while conversions nearly doubled (36 → 65, +81%). Timing email sends after the ID Card arrival clearly amplifies member awareness and conversion.
tests.notes: Source: Iterable campaign data. Metrics collected 1 week after send. 165,255 total EEs in test population.
tests.logCrossRef: Historical Testing Log, Q1 2026 sheet, Test #5: "Email Sent Prior to ID Card Send", Audience: Flight Week #4, Email, Start 1/20 & 1/27, End 2026-02-02, Results Published.

tests.recommendation: Lantern call data largely aligns with Working Planet's reported results. Even accounting for external NC-specific factors, replicating such a return would be highly valuable. The data supports continued investment in Paid Ads and potentially making the NCSHP campaign evergreen, with an expectation of significant incremental revenue and a highly desirable ROAS.

tests.name: ID Card Insert: Impact on Call Rates
tests.testType: Directional / Observational (statistically significant, but not randomized)
tests.summary: Mandatory insert clients vs. carve-out (no insert) clients.
keyTakeaways: Mandatory inserts drove 37% more incremental calls per member mailed vs. carve-outs
Result is statistically significant (p < 0.0001) — extremely unlikely due to chance
Methodology: weighted average (total calls ÷ total mail count per group) gives every member equal weight
Caveat: observational, not randomized. Describes a strong association; unmeasured confounders cannot be ruled out

tests.name: Spouse Mailer Directional Results
tests.summary: Methodology note: 30d pre-period contaminated by Q1 ID Card send. Used 28-day post-mailer window vs. 29d+ settled baseline instead. 4 clients excluded (inflated carry-over activity). n = 155 clients.

headlineMetrics.label: Call Volume Lift (28d window)
headlineMetrics.detail: Average 2.32 calls/day vs. 2.12 baseline; 81% of clients higher call rate; median +0.24 calls/client/day

headlineMetrics.label: Spouse Share Increase
headlineMetrics.detail: 17% → 24% of inbound calls from spouses pre vs post; 63% of clients saw spouse share rise

headlineMetrics.label: Clients with Higher Call Rate
headlineMetrics.detail: 81% directional positive (vs. 17% negative); median client-level change +4.4 ppt spouse share

whySpouseShareMatters: Controls for prior mailer effect: if the ID card mailer drove calls, total volume rises but spouse/self mix stays flat.
Spouse share specifically increased — direct signal the mailer reached its intended audience.
Broad-based result (63% of clients) — not skewed by 1–2 large clients.
caveats: Pre/post volume comparison excluded — prior mailer inflation makes pre-period unreliable.
29d+ baseline is only 21–23 days per client — results will sharpen as more time accumulates.
Covers mailers sent through March 6, 2026; later sends excluded (insufficient post-period).
ELPASOCO, RRISD, BREVARDCOUNTY, Brevard — 29d+ avg rates 10–40x their 28d rates, driven by concurrent OE activity, not mailer response
tests.bottomLine: Spouse mailer performed on both dimensions — call volume up +9.6% (81% of clients) and spouse share up +7.3 ppt (63% of clients). Results are directional; baseline will mature over coming weeks.
